subject: Can I do this with ggplot2

messages.author: 9a5ecf22195d9eb0
messages.subject: Can I do this with ggplot2
parts:
Hey Gguys/Ggals,

I wanted to start learning how to use ggplot2 and thought I'd try to
redo some functionality found in an existing package (GenomeGraphs)
using ggplot as an exploratory exercise.

The most simple type of pictures that I'm trying to make look like
this:

http://cbio.mskcc.org/~lianos/files/ggplot2/sample.png

* The x axis are positions on the genome.
* I have a 4 vectors that have some real valued number for each
position in the genome, plotted in the Samples1..4 lanes.
* The bottom part (blue boxes) are just the positions of where the
"known" genes are on the same genomic coordinates (see how the real
valued numbers in sample1..4 align pretty well w/ positions of known
gene annotations)

Currently GenomeGraphs is implemented using grid graphics. I'm
wondering if ggplot2 has facilities to control the positions of where
to plot things sufficiently enough to try to attempt a graph like this
using ggplot2 functions.

Just curios if trying this is possible and would be a fruitful
endeavor. Again, I'm not trying to redo the entire package, but simply
trying to get facility with ggplot2 to see what it can do.

Thanks,
-steve

messages.author: 5a1b5a9591c118ef
messages.subject: Re: Can I do this with ggplot2
parts:
Hi,

Quick thoughts looking at the package:

- it makes heavy use of S4 methods, which means that if you want to
use its internal objects you may have to write new methods

- supposing you have the data available in data.frames, the graph you
show seems doable in ggplot2 (certainly the top and bottom parts
anyway). However you won't have as much freedom as with grid graphics
should you need to do some fancy positioning like that weird axis in
the middle.

Best,

baptiste
